notes: Flagged large unit checked: `אִטֵּר יַד־יְמִינוֹ` → *left handed*. No morpheme owns a part of the compound — *left* inverts `יְמִין` rather than rendering it, and `אִטֵּר` alone is not *left* — so the four-morpheme grouping is retained as genuinely indivisible. Rule 6's first-token fallback stands because the rendering is a fixed English compound writing no morpheme's lexeme in particular; the competing target head *handed*, which does carry `יָד`, is named in the unit's note.
*Benjamite* fuses `בֶּן` with the gentilic while the separately segmented article keeps the written *the*, exactly as rule 30 reads `דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים` → *chronicles*.
*But when* is one rendering of the single waw (rule 55); the apodosis waw is unrepresented.
